title: Pegatron drives Scope 3 decarbonization through digital platforms, supplier engagement
snippet: Scope 3 emissions are emerging as a major test of corporate management capabilities, requiring companies to move beyond carbon accounting and translate data into measurable supply chain action. Taiwan's Pegatron is tackling the challenge through digital tools, targeted supplier engagement, and collaborative decarbonization initiatives, said Min-hsiang Chen, senior manager at Pegatron's Quality and Sustainability Development Center, at the 2026 Net-Zero Sustainability Summit on November 4.

title: Samsung reportedly plans 2nm fab to boost HBM base-die output
snippet: Samsung Electronics is preparing to build a 2nm- and 4nm-class foundry fab at its Giheung campus in Yongin, South Korea, to expand production of logic base dies used in high-bandwidth memory (HBM). The fab is estimated to cost KRW25 trillion (approx. US$18.6 billion), with the broader project potentially reaching KRW30 trillion if an existing production line is converted into an advanced packaging facility, Seoul Economic Daily reported on November 4.

title: Taiwan digs deep: 2,049-meter geothermal well strikes 140°C in Taitung
snippet: Taiwan's deep geothermal sector is reporting fresh progress after a 2,049-meter well that reached temperatures of 140 degrees Celsius was completed in a challenging metamorphic rock zone in the eastern county of Taitung. The breakthrough strengthens the case for deep geothermal energy as a valuable baseload renewable power source alongside solar and offshore wind.

title: SK Hynix leads HBM4 yield at 60%, expands DRAM supply
snippet: SK Hynix's sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM4) yield has reportedly reached the mid-60% range, the highest in the industry. Analysts say improved yield has lifted production efficiency, allowing the company to expand server DRAM supply even as it concentrates capacity on HBM, a trend also reflected in the growth of its DRAM capacity disclosed in its financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

title: Arm reports record fiscal 2Q27 revenue on licensing momentum and AGI CPU demand
snippet: Arm delivered a record-breaking second quarter for fiscal year 2027, reporting total revenue of US$1.44 billion, up 27% year-over-year. This milestone marks the company's fifth straight quarter of growth exceeding 20%, driven by massive acceleration in its licensing business and strong demand for its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

title: Inventec server demand drives record 10-month revenue

Revenue for the first 10 months totaled NT$822.23 billion, up 43.1% year-over-year, also marking a record high for the period.

title: Syntec Technology's new factories in India, Malaysia to push capacity to more than double in 2027
snippet: Syntec Technology is actively advancing its global production capacity expansion and artificial intelligence (AI) technology deployment. The company announced on November 4 that its Suzhou Plant 2 in China, Malaysia Plant 2, and new facilities in India are expected to be completed and begin relocation in phases starting in February 2027. As the new sites gradually become operational, the company expects its overall capacity in 2027 to reach roughly 2.6 times its current level.

title: QuantumDiamonds targets HBM defects as it develops inline inspection tool
snippet: German quantum-sensing startup QuantumDiamonds has tested its technology on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) devices, including cases involving individual through-silicon via (TSV) failures, as it works to bring its chip defect detection technology into semiconductor production lines. The company, however, does not yet have a high-throughput wafer inspection system.

title: CXMT prepayments surge 16x with DRAM shortage lifting market share
snippet: Global memory supply constraints are creating opportunities for Chinese DRAM maker CXMT to expand its market share. As major international manufacturers prioritise high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced DRAM, the tightening supply of mainstream DRAM is allowing CXMT to capitalise on domestic demand and capacity expansion.

title: AI doubts mount, but server supply chain still sees strong demand
snippet: As concerns over AI deepen and negative headlines continue to emerge, companies across the AI server supply chain say customer orders remain strong. Industry sources said Nvidia GPU servers are entering a transition phase between old and new platforms. However, ASIC servers are filling the gap, supporting a positive outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026 as Nvidia's Vera Rubin shipments gradually ramp up in the first quarter of 2027.

title: Anthropic's Claude reportedly cuts custom chip design timelines with a 15-person team

It and another frontier lab, OpenAI, are beginning to probe the AI-assisted chip design market as a new business area, even as they seek to produce their own silicon.
